QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_22

question.text: In the context of a Category II PE fund, the 'J-curve' refers to:

answer.text: The trajectory of management fees over fund life
The shape of the fund's asset allocation chart
The steep initial drop in IRR during vintage years followed by recovery and peak returns near maturity
The relationship between hurdle rate and catch-up rate

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.7.3: J-curve reflects negative cash flows in initial years (fees and expenses outstrip distributions as investments are being made), followed by positive cash flows and rising IRR as exits materialise. Typical pattern for Cat I/II AIFs. The Trap: Options B, C, D are unrelated constructs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B tests J-curve; XXI-B covers it for illiquid PMS strategies. Manager's Pro-Tip: When reporting interim IRRs to LPs during vintage years, always contextualise against the J-curve — otherwise LPs panic over negative Year 2 IRRs. Include a historical J-curve overlay of comparable vintage funds in quarterly updates.
